01

Printed Community Diorama

The default plan, built, by dayOpen

An interactive model of a master-planned community that builds itself on screen: raw land, roads, lots, slabs, printed walls, roofs and landscape, with the printer at work. A nine-step walkthrough takes a developer through the pro forma layer by layer, and three tours show the same plan from the builder's, the general contractor's and the hospitality operator's seat.

A community you already know how to build. One change: the walls are printed.

04

How the work is made

Every tool here is built the same way: on one register of facts, one design system and one set of checks.

Sourced, or marked as a thesis

Every figure links to its source or is labeled a thesis. When the evidence is unsure, the work uses the figure that is worse for the idea.

In the model, each line of the pro forma is tagged Published or Thesis.

Plain words

Short sentences and real estate terms. Each idea comes down to one sentence and the one fact that carries it.

The Rolodex screens each firm on three counts: repetition, printer fit, and a record of paying for a new building method.

Dense, but not invasive

Little opens by itself, and nothing advances on its own. Everything is there for whoever looks.

The model opens on the plan, two buttons and one sentence. Behind them: 11 plan layouts in 15 regions, a walkthrough and three tours.

Checked before it ships

Figures are checked against the bytes of each cited page, links for status, copy for banned words, and every view at phone and desktop width in both themes.

Bedrock, the design system

Bedrock is where the guidelines behind these tools are gathered, so each deliverable can be produced again, the same way, for any firm. It holds the page components, the rules for copy, sourcing and figures, and one register with the wording for every fact that more than one tool states.

  • Figures, checked against the bytes of each cited page
  • Links, checked for status and banned hosts
  • Copy, checked against a list of banned words and em dashes
  • Every view opened at phone and desktop width, in both themes

Four of its rules, with their sources

Compare by position on a common scale: bars, dots and ranges, not pies or bubbles.

Cleveland and McGill, 1984

A figure's title says what is drawn. The finding goes in the reading under it.

Kong, Liu and Karahalios, 2018

A strip of about four numbers, a view of four or five steps.

Cowan, 2001

No mono text under 11px, no reading text under 12.5px.

Legge and Bigelow, 2011
